solution.summary: Empire State Development (ESD) receives a single, integrated AI Prep program built and delivered by a lead administrator that designs the curriculum, recruits and supports participants, and places them into paid internships (Track A) and full-time AI jobs (Track B). The solution is a build-and-operate engagement: curriculum and assessment assets are developed in a mobilisation phase, then cohorts are recruited, trained online, coached and placed across the 18-month initial term beginning January 1, 2026, with a data and reporting spine running throughout. Delivery is organised in four phases — mobilise and finalise design, recruit and launch the first cohort, deliver and place at scale, and sustain and report — each with monthly milestones and performance estimates against ESD's three metrics. The team is a lead administrator with a program director, curriculum and instructional design staff, employer partnership leads, success coaches and a compliance/reporting function, supported by named subcontractors for outreach and employer engagement. Pricing is built bottom-up within the $2M per track / $4M total cap, with stipends and wraparound supports as explicit budget lines and no indirect costs. Governance, MWBE/SDVOB participation, insurance and contract compliance are handled by a dedicated compliance workstream that runs from proposal submission through quarterly and monthly reporting.

components.title: Program design, curriculum and assessment build
components.description: We design an industry-informed AI curriculum built with employer and researcher input, delivered as online courses with defined technical skills and learning milestones (R014, R025). The build covers the full AI technology training program for low-income college students including the internship component (R009), the accelerated bootcamp alternative to a degree for Track B (R007), and the immersive schedule that can run part-time or full-time (R027). We define the credentials awarded on completion (R031) and embed skill-attainment evaluation metrics at each milestone (R029). The curriculum is developed in the mobilisation phase and refreshed each cohort against employer feedback, and the whole delivery plan is scoped to the 18-month initial term with any renewal or extension treated as a separately priced option (R035).

claims.text: ESD has no AI Prep program today; OSWD is launching it as a new applied training program and will award contracts to up to two program administrators to develop the curriculum and administer it.
The anticipated contract start date is January 1, 2026, with an initial term of up to 18 months and possible renewal or extension based on performance, need and availability of funds.

components.title: Outreach, recruitment and eligibility assessment
components.description: We run a targeted outreach and recruitment strategy for low-income students and for unemployed, underemployed and underrepresented New Yorkers (R011, R024), reaching New Yorkers underrepresented in tech who cannot reasonably access training on their own (R008). A structured application and evaluation process screens and selects participants (R012), and a needs assessment at intake identifies and addresses each participant's barriers to success (R013). Track A recruitment targets low-income matriculating undergraduates (R006); Track B recruitment targets low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment (R007).

claims.text: ESD's stated pain point is that many well-paying AI jobs require specialised education that lower-income New Yorkers cannot access, and that recruiting favours elite-school students and personal connections.

components.title: Training delivery, coaching and participant supports
components.description: We deliver and manage the AI training program cohort by cohort (R015), with professional development support for trainees throughout training (R030). Every participant receives a stipend and wraparound supports including mentors and career coaches with industry expertise (R016), and the budget carries the proposed stipend level and wraparound supports as explicit lines (R051). Track A students are trained specifically to secure paid internships at leading tech companies (R006, R021), and Track B participants are connected to full-time AI jobs through the accelerated pathway (R007, R032).

claims.text: Deliverables common to both tracks include participant stipends and wrap-around supports such as mentors or success coaches.

components.title: Employer partnerships and placement engine
components.description: We cultivate and maintain relationships with leading industry employers to inform training content and generate paid internship opportunities (R018), and we help students secure paid internships (R017). Internships are structured so students hone newly acquired AI skills through real-world experience and networking that leads to full-time roles (R022), and we provide full-time job connection support in AI-related fields (R032). The program creates direct education-to-industry pathways and builds a talent pipeline for AI employers (R010), with placement support tailored to New York State technology companies (R021).

claims.text: The majority of program graduates must secure paid internships or full-time employment in AI or a closely related field.

components.title: Performance measurement, data tracking and ESD reporting
components.description: We stand up a data system that tracks and records information relevant to grant success (R056) and makes it available to ESD on request (R057). The tracked data set covers applicant counts and low-income percentages, enrollment and completion counts with low-income percentages, paid internship and full-time placement rates with low-income percentages, participating colleges and universities, and participating employer partners (R058). We estimate annual performance on total participants served, low-income completion percentage and placement rate, justified by historical results and partner commitments (R090), and we report against the 250-participant minimum, the over-50% low-income target and the majority-placement target (R038, R040, R041).

claims.text: Awarded administrators must track and report applicant, enrollment and completion counts with low-income percentages, placement rates, participating colleges and employer partners, with the exact list set during contract negotiation.
The program must serve a minimum of 250 participants, with priority for proposals serving more than 400, and over 50% of participants must be low-income.

components.title: Budget, pricing and cost justification
components.description: We submit a line-by-line price proposal for fees (R091), with Personnel Services broken out by job title, named employee where known, hourly or annual rate, fringe rate, percentage of time and cost to contract (R092), and Other Than Personnel Services on separate lines showing cost to contract and quantity (R093). The budget is mapped to the program duration and includes staff salary and benefits, wraparound supports and the proposed stipend level (R049, R050, R051), plus other costs such as curriculum development, marketing and events (R052). It is built within the $2M per track and $4M total cap (R034), excludes indirect costs (R053), states the extent of any cost match in the budget template (R054), and carries a written justification (R047).

claims.text: ESD will invest up to $2M per track, up to $4M total, to train and provide stipends for participants, and indirect costs are not allowable.

components.title: Program governance, staffing and contract compliance
components.description: We designate a single lead organisation for the programming (R043) and field a team whose experience covers at least three of the four required domains — academic services to college students, high-tech accelerated training, serving low-income populations and the New York market (R045) — backed by a track record in AI or similar workforce development (R042) and the financial ability, organisational capacity and legal authority to perform (R165). The lead entity is a for-profit corporation, which satisfies the requirement that the applicant be a non-profit or for-profit entity (R044). Staff assigned to the project are submitted for ESD approval (R139), we notify ESD immediately of proposed staff changes and provide each substitute's experience summary and an interview before approval (R141, R142), and we commit to staff continuity through completion (R140). We represent that all personnel possess the required experience and character (R143), that staff hold required qualifications, training, licences and permits (R147), are legally entitled to work (R148) and comply with federal and state employment law (R149). The contract is not assigned or transferred (R144), and no subcontracting occurs beyond what the proposal identifies without prior written approval of the State Project Manager (R146). We perform to applicable professional standards (R134), correct patent errors at no charge (R135), assert any change-related claim within 30 days of written notice (R136), continue performance while a claim is pending (R137), and keep additional services within the contract's general scope and outside licensed professional work (R138). We accept Schedule A and provide any information ESD requests under it (R107, R250), acknowledge that the contract is unenforceable until OSC review and approval under Public Authorities Law §2879-a (R133), and accept that proposal costs are borne by us (R131) and that response information may be retained and used by ESD (R132).

claims.text: Contractor staff are subject to ESD approval, staff continuity is expected through project completion, and subcontracting not identified in the proposal requires prior written approval of the State Project Manager.

components.title: Ethics, integrity and responsibility compliance
components.description: We observe the restricted period, contacting only the designated ESD contacts until contract approval (R001), and we do not offer gifts to ESD employees, members or directors (R153) or discuss employment with ESD personnel involved in the procurement within 30 days of their involvement closing (R154). We attest to the Conflict of Interest provisions (R152) and disclose any existing or contemplated relationship that could be an actual or potential conflict or appearance of impropriety (R155). We update the State Finance Law 139-j/139-k disclosure and affirmation forms periodically during the term (R162) and accept sole responsibility for full compliance with those Procurement Requirements (R164). We demonstrate integrity and satisfactory performance on prior government contracts (R166, R167), register in the Vend-Rep System (R168), review EO-192 vendor integrity requirements (R175), certify compliance with EO-16 on Russia (R177) and with the Human Rights Law including reasonable accommodation (R179), and certify no collusion under Public Authorities Law §2878 (R150).

claims.text: The procurement is subject to a restricted period under the Procurement Lobbying Law running until contract approval, during which respondents may contact only the designated contacts Julia Borukhov and Jordan Kaplan at AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov.

components.title: MWBE and SDVOB participation and diversity reporting
components.description: We document good faith efforts to give MWBEs meaningful subcontracting and supplier participation (R181) against ESD's 30% overall MWBE goal (R182), counting only sums paid for a commercially useful function (R184) and applying the 25% broker rule for non-construction contracts (R185). We accept that ESD may withhold payment pending MWBE documentation (R183), that willful failure to meet the goals is a breach with liquidated damages equal to the shortfall against sums identified for MWBE payment (R187, R188), and we evidence good faith efforts through the New York State Contract System (R189). We report any post-award change to the MWBE Utilization Plan on a revised plan for ESD approval (R192), file any post-award waiver request no later than before the final payment request (R197), and accept Schedule B in full (R200). We submit quarterly Workforce Utilization Reports (R203), require the same of subcontractors (R204), report gross wages per employee quarterly under EO #162 (R205), and do not discriminate on Human Rights Law grounds (R207). Because our scope is AI training and placement rather than construction, demolition, repair, renovation, planning or design of real property, the construction-scoped equal employment opportunity programme obligation does not attach to our subcontracts; we nonetheless flow down our non-discrimination and EEO policy to every subcontractor so that minority group members and women are afforded equal opportunity without discrimination (R201). For SDVOBs we document good faith efforts (R212), report post-award changes on a revised SDVOB Utilization Plan (R215), follow the submitted plan (R222) and accept that failure to use SDVOBs as agreed is a material breach (R223). We speak with the Designated Contacts before any waiver request (R224), attempt in good faith to use the SDVOBs in our plan (R227), and keep evidence of good faith efforts: solicitations and responses (R233), reasons each responding SDVOB was not selected (R234), dates of ESD-scheduled SDVOB meetings attended (R235) and steps taken to structure the scope for SDVOB subcontracting (R236). We file Monthly SDVOB Contractor Compliance reports by the 10th of each month to OCSD@esd.ny.gov (R237, R239) and accept damages for willful non-compliance (R240). We consider SDVOBs in subcontracting, supply and partnering roles (R210), reference the OGS SDVOB directory (R211) and consider New York State businesses generally (R241).

claims.text: The contract carries a 30% MWBE participation goal and a 6% SDVOB participation goal, requiring MWBE and SDVOB Utilization Plans with the proposal and quarterly and monthly compliance reporting thereafter.

components.title: Insurance, tax certification and contract administration
components.description: We carry Commercial General Liability of $1M per occurrence and $2M aggregate (R251), Commercial Automobile of $1M where a vehicle is used (R252), Sexual Abuse and Molestation insurance of $1M (R253), and Workers' Compensation and Employer's Liability (R254) and Disability coverage (R255) at State statutory limits. ESD is named additional insured on a primary and non-contributory basis on the GL and Auto policies (R256), and all required policies carry a waiver of subrogation in favour of ESD (R257). We periodically update the certifications in Form ST-220-CA during the contract term (R247).

claims.text: The selected respondent must carry Commercial General Liability of $1M per occurrence and $2M aggregate, Commercial Auto of $1M if a vehicle is used, Sexual Abuse and Molestation insurance of $1M, and statutory Workers' Compensation, Employer's Liability and Disability coverage, naming ESD as additional insured with a waiver of subrogation.

components.title: Procurement communications and post-award administration
components.description: We manage every procurement communication through the designated channel: all questions about the RFP are submitted by email to AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov by the August 29, 2025 deadline (R060), and we accept that questions submitted after the deadline given in the Schedule of Dates may not be answered (R128). We review ESD's posted responses of September 12, 2025 before finalising the proposal. After award, if we are unsuccessful we request a debriefing within 15 calendar days of ESD's notification that our proposal was not selected (R259), and if we are successful we hold the contract on the 18-month initial term with renewal or extension at ESD's discretion based on performance, need and availability of funds (R035).

claims.text: Questions are due by email to AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov by August 29, 2025, with ESD responses due September 12, 2025, proposals due 2:00 PM ET on October 1, 2025, and the successful respondent announced November 14, 2025.

assumptions.text: The bid is submitted for both tracks under one lead administrator, with a single program management office and shared services, priced at no more than $2M per track and $4M in total.

Low-income eligibility is defined as Pell-grant eligibility for Track A and household income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level for Track B, verified by documentation at application, subject to ESD's confirmation at contract negotiation.

Participant stipends are paid from the administrator's award budget, while internship wages are paid by host employers, and the stipend is set at a per-participant rate that leaves the majority of the $2M per track for training delivery and supports.

The program is sized at approximately 400 participants per track over the 18-month term, in cohorts of 50 running on a rolling part-time and full-time schedule, which is the basis for staffing and unit costs.
The budget is mapped to the 18-month initial term from January 1, 2026, and any renewal or extension is priced separately at the same unit rates rather than assumed in the base price.

A graduate is a participant who completes all curriculum milestones and the final assessment, and placement is measured as paid internship or full-time AI-related employment secured within six months of completion.

The final reporting data set and reporting frequency will be fixed at contract negotiation, and the solution is built on a configurable data model so added fields and cadences do not require re-platforming.

The Appendix A ESD IT Security Standard Brief and Appendix B Diversity Practices Questionnaire will be obtained from ESD and applied as issued, with the platform configured to meet Appendix A controls and the questionnaire completed from our existing diversity practices record.
The cost-match credit is pursued through a modest documented cash and in-kind match shown in the budget template, on the basis that the RFP gives no scoring formula for match.

The 30% MWBE and 6% SDVOB goals are treated as applying to total contract value and as requiring demonstrated good faith efforts rather than guaranteed attainment, with waiver requests filed on Form OCSD-5 only after consulting the Designated Contacts.

OSC review under Public Authorities Law §2879-a is assumed to apply given the award size, so mobilisation is planned to begin on award with curriculum build completing before the January 1, 2026 start and no reliance on pre-approval spend.

All subcontractors, including outreach partners and employer engagement specialists, are named in the proposal with scope and estimated value so the proposal-identified subcontracting exception applies without further written approval.

The Technical Proposal carries a Cost of Services section limited to the line-by-line price schedule requested, resolving the tension with the instruction not to include information beyond what is requested.
Schedule A concerns are submitted in writing with the Administrative Proposal and Schedule A documentation itself is kept out of the proposal, so both instructions are satisfied.

The construction-scoped equal employment opportunity programme obligation is treated as not attaching to this AI training and placement scope, with our non-discrimination and EEO policy flowed down to all subcontractors instead.
